title: Spark Savings v2 inverts the schema by recording an Asset Supplied By Users, so one template covers both outbound allocation and inbound deposits
content:
Every instance up to this point has carried the field `Asset Supplied By Spark Liquidity Layer`. The Spark Savings v2 instances replace it with `Asset Supplied By Users`: wETH for the ETH instance (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.9.1.2.1.3), USDC (.9.2.2.1.3) and USDT (.9.3.2.1.3), each paired with a receipt token — spETH, spUSDC, spUSDT — and a `Target Protocol` of "Spark Savings Protocol".

The direction of capital reverses. In a SparkLend or Aave instance the Spark Liquidity Layer is the depositor and an external protocol is the venue. Here the public is the depositor and Spark is the venue: these are Spark's own savings products, registered in the same Allocation System Primitive tree, under the same `Active` status, with the same document shape.

Unifying both under one registry is a real design position. It means the Artifact holds a single inventory of everywhere value flows through Spark, whether outward into third-party protocols or inward from users, and one governance process amends both.

It also means a single field name is the only thing distinguishing 'Spark is the counterparty taking risk' from 'Spark is the counterparty others take risk on'. Everything downstream differs — the relevant controls, who is protected, what failure looks like — yet the structural signal is one word in one slot. A reader scanning `Asset Supplied By...` values without reading the field name would classify these instances exactly backwards.
description: Where every other instance names the Asset Supplied By Spark Liquidity Layer, the Savings instances name what users deposit
